title: Segal homotopy categories and invariance of invertibility along arrow components
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, components and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and Reedy fibrancy from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $W:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be Reedy fibrant, and suppose that each consecutive-edge map $W_n\to W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for $n\geq2$. For vertices $x,y\in W_0$, let $M_W(x,y)$ be the strict fiber of $(d_1,d_0):W_1\to W_0^2$. The objects $x\in(W_0)_0$, morphism sets $\pi_0M_W(x,y)$, identities represented by $s_0x$, and composition obtained by lifting two consecutive arrows to $W_2$ and applying $d_1$ form a well-defined unital associative category $hW$. Every map of such simplicial spaces induces a functor on these categories by its maps on objects and mapping spaces.

If vertices $g,g'\in W_1$ belong to the same path component of $W_1$, then the class of $g$ is an isomorphism in $hW$ if and only if the class of $g'$ is an isomorphism in $hW$, even when their source and target vertices differ. Consequently, if $W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the union of components of $W_1$ that contain an isomorphism, then every vertex of $W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ represents an isomorphism, and its strict fiber at $(x,y)$ is precisely the union of the isomorphism components of $M_W(x,y)$.

source.place: Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Sections 5.1-5.7, Proposition 5.4 and Lemma 5.8, printed pp. 11-14. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this Segal-space result.
